svg.title: Sampling turns a continuous wave into a list of numbers
svg.desc: Top: a continuous sound wave with a slow pattern and fast wiggles is measured at regular, closely spaced moments. Each dot is one sample, and the time between samples is T, which equals one divided by the sampling rate. At 16,000 samples per second, T is 0.0625 milliseconds. Bottom: the same wave measured too rarely. Joining the dots keeps the slow pattern but loses the fast wiggles. A sampling rate can only capture frequencies up to half its value, the Nyquist frequency.

g.text: Sampling: from a smooth wave to numbers
Enough samples: the shape is kept
Too few samples: the fast wiggles are lost
